run.question: Which spawned children write their own report, ledger, fragment or evidence file today (among them the adversary's {slug}-adversary.md, an /afk:investigate run's REPORT.md and COVERAGE.json, and each tracer's fragment), who starts each and how the starter reads that file, and what breaks if, with no pane transport or with the switch set back to subagents, such a child returns its report text and the agent that started it writes the file? Premise: At review:38, diagnose:83 and to-prd:12 the invoking agent runs /afk:investigate inline; the L9 seam runs are the grill-solution premise runs that S-208 counts as role spawns. Premise: The fallback moves the report writes of 3 kinds of role child only; afk-runner helpers keep writing evidence files. Premise: Every page writer on the authored path, the /afk:prototype one included, is a pane role agent with lifespan Feature that writes its page. Premise: Under the fallback, the starter writes the returned adversary report to the named path before it cites any finding. Premise: A helper never runs /afk:investigate; it returns open code claims as unverified, and its pane-agent starter investigates them. Premise: The mutation-probe output of a review worker is build output, not a report file; the fallback leaves it with the worker. Premise: The retester writes only its result file; the main /afk:bug session copies the evidence into the bug directory and records the path.

nodes.evidence: The plan is the load-bearing interface between `/afk:to-subtasks` (emitter) and `/afk:execute` (parser + progress writer). A subtask's **id** is its filename stem (`NNNN-slug`); no Jira keys in the plan. Adding/renaming/changing a section → update **both** `skills/afk/to-subtasks/SKILL.md` ("Subtask contract" emitter) and `skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md` (Step 1 parser) in the same commit — same repo so this lockstep is enforced by one commit. Likewise the outcome status set (now including `adversary_fail`): broadening it → update the status list in `/afk:execute` Step 13 and any skill referencing a status by name. Autopilot's park handling is deliberately status-agnostic — its step 4 parks on anything that is not a recognised success — so a new status needs no edit there, and its absence from `skills/afk/autopilot/SKILL.md` is not drift. Smoke gate has two shapes — full (`## Feature smoke gate`) and minimal (`## Feature smoke gate (minimal)`) — same three-way lockstep: `to-verification-plan` emitter (full only), `to-subtasks` seeder (both, incl. minimal-gate template in its SMOKE-GATE.md), `smoke-test` reader (both). Today three kinds of spawned role child write their own file. The adversary writes plan/review/{NNNN-slug}-adversary.md (skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:40); /afk:execute Step 10.5 starts it in a fresh session or subagent (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:89). A spawned /afk:investigate run copies COVERAGE.json into its ledger directory and writes REPORT.md beside it at step 7 (skills/utils/investigate/SKILL.md:62); /afk:grill-requirements (SKILL.md:46), /afk:grill-solution per premise (SKILL.md:76) and its grounding rule (GROUNDING-RULE.md:25, :40) start these runs in the background. Each afk-tracer writes its fragment at the path its caller names, plus evidence files beside it (agents/afk-tracer.md:16); /afk:investigate step 4 starts the tracers and hands each that path (skills/utils/investigate/SKILL.md:44).

How each starter takes the child's result today: the adversary ends its output with the ADVERSARY verdict line, which names the report path (skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:43); /afk:execute routes on that verdict (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:89-93) and treats medium or low findings as advisories living in plan/review/*.md (:92); no line of /afk:execute names the -adversary.md file. /afk:investigate step 5 folds each fragment from the file path it passes as --fragment (skills/utils/investigate/SKILL.md:45, :49), and the fold loads that path from disk (skills/utils/investigate/scripts/merge_fragments.py:627). A grilling session acts on the ledgers its runs publish (skills/afk/grill-solution/GROUNDING-RULE.md:43).

Every downstream reader found reads these files by path or glob and checks nothing about which agent wrote them: mission control (skills/afk/mission-control/scripts/mc/sections/gates.py:110, insights.py:204, progress.py:75), /afk:retro (skills/afk/retro/SKILL.md:29) and the review rollup (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:167) for the adversary report; the SDD gate (skills/afk/to-sdd/scripts/check_sdd_investigations.py:119), the plan validator (skills/afk/to-subtasks/scripts/validate_plan.py:461) and execute's consumer preflight (skills/afk/execute/CITED-MODE.md:53) for COVERAGE.json; the fold for fragments, whose identity check is the partition and tables (merge_fragments.py:78-89). So they stay unchanged when the starter writes the same content at the same path.

Other spawned children that write or keep files today: the afk-runner and afk-runner-lite helpers write only evidence files and return the path (agents/afk-runner.md:14, agents/afk-runner-lite.md:18, providers/codex/agents/afk-afk-runner.toml:2), started for long-output tiers by /afk:execute (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:67) and per modality by /afk:smoke-test (skills/afk/smoke-test/SKILL.md:43); the page-writer child writes the page markup (LAVISH.md:268, :272, skills/afk/to-meeting-b/SKILL.md:139); the test-veracity review worker runs mutation-probe.sh, which logs to a temp file (skills/afk/review/checklists/test-veracity.md:25, adapters/build-gate/maven/mutation-probe.sh:68). The /afk:bug retester edits no file and returns its evidence as text (skills/afk/bug/RETEST-PROMPT.md:12, :25), and only the main /afk:bug session writes the bug ledger (skills/afk/bug/SKILL.md:30).

Given the premises that afk-runner helpers keep writing evidence files, that every authored-path page writer is a pane role agent with lifespan Feature that writes its page, that a review worker's mutation-probe output is build output left with the worker, and that the retester writes only its result file while the main /afk:bug session copies the evidence, the fallback moves none of the writes in the previous claim: their sites (agents/afk-runner.md:14, LAVISH.md:272, adapters/build-gate/maven/mutation-probe.sh:68, skills/afk/bug/LEDGER-FORMAT.md:80) stay unchanged.

claims.text: Whether a spawned subagent loads the user's steering file that carries the rule to answer code questions with /afk:investigate (skills/afk/setup/INVESTIGATION-SESSIONS.md:17-18) is harness runtime: no repository document states it and no probe row of providers/CONFORMANCE.md:308-330 tests it.

Whether a Claude Code subagent's Write tool refuses the review gate's own files is unproven: under /afk:autopilot the review orchestrator runs inside the subtask subagent (skills/afk/autopilot/SKILL.md:33, skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:71) and writes plan/review/{NNNN-slug}-{base-short}.md, its .findings.json and the rollup plan/review/INDEX.md (skills/afk/review/SKILL.md:157, :159); the probe row tested only REPORT.md, SUMMARY.md and findings.md (refused) and 0001-x-adversary.md, notes.md, fragment.json, COVERAGE.json and evidence.txt (written) (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:329), and the settled rows move none of these writes (docs/afk/agent-team-topology/GRILL-LOG.md:561).

Under docs/, the ledger file name COVERAGE.json occurs on 3 lines of tracked files (research/FACTS-claude.md:85, :86 and research/PROPOSAL-claude.md:104), on no line of the 18 untracked feature files, on 71 lines of the 34 prior REPORT.md files and on no line of INV-002-schema-table/COVERAGE.json; a case-blind rerun of each search returned the same lines. The other 33 prior COVERAGE.json files hold 345828 matching lines, counted and not enumerated, so the hit set for that form is complete under docs/ except in those 33 files.

The settled feature documents name 3 kinds of role child that write their own file today: the adversary writes {slug}-adversary.md and /afk:execute starts it; each /afk:investigate run writes its REPORT.md and ledger, started by /afk:grill-requirements, by /afk:grill-solution and by its grounding rule; each tracer writes its fragment, started by /afk:investigate (GRILL-LOG.md:561, S-209). Under the fallback each such child returns its text and the agent that started it writes the file (GRILL-LOG.md:462, S-157; PRD.md:144, AC-044). Children that edit code or plugin files keep writing, and review concern workers already return their findings (GRILL-LOG.md:561).

In the pane design the documents route a role's result through a file: the started agent writes it to the path its brief names and sends finished with that path (GRILL-LOG.md:459, ROLE-2); the requester picks the path, and a gate names its worker's report file under plan/review/ (GRILL-LOG.md:525, RES-1); only the role's report target reads it (GRILL-LOG.md:674, S-239; PRD.md:149, AC-049). Under the fallback the documents replace that hand-off with the subagent's returned text, which the starter writes to the file (PRD.md:40, PRD.md:144).

Two feature documents still state no behaviour difference where AC-001 now states one. SDD.md:591 sets the count of behaviour differences with no topology entry and no multi-model to 0, citing AC-001, and INDEX.md:3 says that with neither switch turned on nothing changes; AC-001 names one difference, a subagent's report file written by the agent that started it (PRD.md:101, AC-044). The planned change is that difference, so both sentences disagree with the criterion they summarise.

The change has no seam row and is missing from the posture. S-199 classes 'the report-file writers when role agents fall back to subagents' as reworked, a change an existing caller sees (GRILL-LOG.md:551). The SDD's seam table has 13 rows and none for those writers (SDD.md:763-779), and the posture S-246 counts 12 changes, 3 of them seen by an existing caller (the configuration reader, the delegation rules and the Codex agent names), and says a session that uses no team sees no change (GRILL-LOG.md:681). Under AC-001's one difference (PRD.md:101), a session with no team whose role agents fall back to subagents sees this change, so the posture's count and that sentence no longer hold.

In a pattern run on TR-1 the fallback and the result-read rule disagree. Only the contact agent starts a team agent (PRD.md:109, AC-009); under the fallback, patterns run on TR-1 (PRD.md:40); and the agent that started a role subagent writes its report file from the returned text (PRD.md:144, AC-044). So the contact agent would receive every role's report. But a role's result goes only to its report target, by default the agent that asked (PRD.md:148, AC-048; ADR-0015), and the contact agent reads a result only when it is the target (PRD.md:149, AC-049; PRD.md:174; GRILL-LOG.md:674, S-239). None of these rows names an exception for the fallback.

The feature documents state the refusal more broadly than the probe row. GRILL-LOG.md:166 says a subagent cannot write a report file, ADR-0013 says the harness refuses it, and PRD.md:258 records that Claude Code refuses a report file written by a subagent. The probe row saw the Claude Code Write tool refuse only REPORT.md, SUMMARY.md and findings.md, while the same subagent wrote 0001-x-adversary.md, fragment.json, COVERAGE.json and evidence.txt, wrote bash-REPORT.md through the shell, and a Codex sub-agent was refused nothing (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:329). The R-16 trigger was one refused REPORT.md write (GRILL-LOG.md:160).

RPW-1 (S-209) sorts the role spawns into 3 moved kinds, 5 code or plugin-file writers that keep writing, and the review concern workers that already return (GRILL-LOG.md:561). At least six role spawns of CLS-1 (S-208) are in none of those lists: the /afk:review skeptics and adjudicators, the /afk:understand skeptic, the /afk:verify-seams blind verifier, and the /afk:bug publisher and retester (GRILL-LOG.md:560).

Given the premise that the fallback moves the report writes of 3 kinds of role child only, the /afk:bug publisher and retester, which return their result line through a result file (GRILL-LOG.md:491, S-165; GRILL-LOG.md:459, ROLE-2), keep writing that file when they run as subagents. Whether a Claude Code subagent may write it is unproven: the probe row tested other file names only (providers/CONFORMANCE.md:329).

How a subagent's final text reaches the agent that started it, and how much text one reply carries, is harness runtime that no feature document states. A case-blind search of GRILL-LOG.md, INDEX.md, LAVISH-TIPS.md, PRD.md, SDD.md, adr/ and research/ for final text, truncation and reply bounds found the fallback's own statements (GRILL-LOG.md:166, PRD.md:40, PRD.md:144) and bounds for other transports only: a desktop-tool headless run's output of about 100,000 characters (research/FACTS-codex.md:52) and a Codex non-interactive run's final message on stdout (research/EVIDENCE-codex-providers.md:25). AC-044 routes every report, ledger and fragment through that reply (PRD.md:144).

Given the premise that only report, ledger and fragment writes move, the stall watchdog keeps its sign of life: a tracer still writes evidence files, and a fire reads the task-output tail before parking (hooks/stall-watchdog.sh:13-24, DELEGATION.md:37).
